title: Australia probes flydubai co-pilot links, police say
gist: Australia's Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team is investigating the 'links to Australia' of Hammam al-Hammami, the Omani co-pilot identified by sources as having attacked the captain of flydubai flight 1073 to Tel Aviv with a crash axe in what the UAE called a 'terrorist attack'; he reportedly studied in Melbourne and, per the FT, allegedly visited radical mosques and extremist websites, with Australian intelligence holding a file on him.

insights.claim: The co-pilot of flydubai flight 1073 from Dubai to Israel attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, an incident the UAE prosecutor general called a 'terrorist attack'.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Framing as terrorism elevates security scrutiny of Gulf-Israel air links and airline crew vetting.
insights.quote: attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe
insights.locator: The co-pilot of the flydubai flight 1073

insights.claim: Two sources identified the co-pilot as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national; UAE and Omani authorities have not confirmed or commented, and flydubai says a full investigation is under way.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Official silence leaves open diplomatic and liability questions for Oman, the UAE and the airline.
insights.locator: The co-pilot of the flydubai jet was identified

insights.claim: The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team — comprising the AFP, Victoria Police and ASIO — confirmed it is investigating the co-pilot's links to Australia.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Involvement of a counterterror task force indicates authorities are treating possible radicalization networks seriously.
insights.quote: can confirm it is investigating the man's links to Australia

insights.claim: Two sources said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne; local media named RMIT, which declined to comment.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Shows the cross-border paths in pilot training that complicate airline background vetting.
insights.locator: Two sources briefed on the investigation

insights.claim: The Financial Times reported, citing two people familiar with the investigation, that al-Hammami allegedly visited radical mosques and extremist websites while in Australia and that Australian intelligence held a file on him; Reuters could not verify this.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: If confirmed, a known-to-intelligence individual reaching an airline cockpit would point to information-sharing gaps between intelligence services and foreign carriers.
insights.quote: al-Hammami had allegedly visited radical mosques and extremist websites while in Australia
insights.locator: The Financial Times reported on Sunday
